patient._comment: 'patient' contains the three sections that may be exposed in the detailed patient display: presentation, answer, and clinical.

presentation._comment: The immutable patient evidence package available for triage. Panel context controls whether other sections are locked or available.
presentation.quote: I was so close to landing the kickflip. My wrist bent weird and crunched, and now it hurts to twist it. Can I still skate this weekend?
presentation.triageNote: 9-year-old boy after a fall onto an outstretched hand from a skateboard, with focal distal-forearm tenderness, subtle dorsal angulation, and pain with wrist rotation. Finger movement and distal circulation and sensation are intact.

answer._comment: The authoritative game answer. Explicit ESI, destination, and destination rationale are answer-bearing content; the player's assignment remains session state.
answer.destinationReason: ESI 4 is appropriate because this stable isolated wrist injury is expected to require one resource: an X-ray.

clinical._comment: Display-ready clinical interpretation derived from patient.presentation. It preserves clinical meaning but must not explicitly name or identify the correct ESI level or destination; it does not participate in scoring.
clinical.summary: This is a stable child with an isolated distal-forearm injury and intact distal neurovascular function.
clinical.acuityReason: Focal tenderness and subtle angulation make a fracture likely, but there is no open injury, severe deformity, or neurovascular compromise.
keyFindings: Intact finger movement, circulation, and sensation
teachingPoints: Subtle deformity after a fall can indicate a stable pediatric fracture even when finger movement is preserved.
Splinting is treatment rather than an additional diagnostic resource in the resource-count step.

possibleClinicalOutcome.disposition: Imaging would likely be followed by splinting and outpatient follow-up, with discharge precautions for increasing pain, swelling, numbness, or color change.

aiImageGeneration._comment: 'aiImageGeneration' is info for AI to generate the image of the patient. Most images were done with openAI gpt-image-1 using an API, not the app, in July 2026. Look for some python scripts that are used to create these images. Be sure that the anchor-image is available and is provided to the AI - otherwise the images will not be consistent.
aiImageGeneration.who: 9-year-old boy in skate gear (helmet, knee pads), skateboard propped beside him
aiImageGeneration.pose: sitting, cradling his right forearm against his body
aiImageGeneration.expression: pouty but tough, a mild wince
aiImageGeneration.prompt: Softly-shaded painterly cartoon illustration in a semi-realistic Pixar/Disney style: smooth gradient shading, soft natural lighting, gentle rounded volumes, fine delicate outlines (NOT thick flat cartoon outlines), warm detailed rendering, natural realistic proportions, single character, 3/4 front view, centered, square 1:1. Match the exact painterly style, brushwork, shading, line weight, lighting, and palette of the attached reference image. Subject: a white 9-year-old boy in skate gear (helmet, knee pads), a skateboard propped beside him, seated on a blue padded clinic chair. Pose: sitting, cradling his right forearm against his body. Expression: pouty but tough, a mild wince. Clearly visible: cradling the right forearm, slight swelling at the wrist. No text, no logos.
